Could meditation unveil a hidden SU(3) symmetry linking mind and cosmos?

#QuantumPhysics #ConsciousnessScience

NASA rovers on Moon and Mars: Curiosity and Perseverance lead in distance, as of Oct. 2026. Explore their journey!

#Rovers #SpaceExploration

NASA seeks legal professionals for the Office of the General Counsel—join our mission in space and law!

#NASAJobs #LegalCareers

🎬 New Short: A teaspoon of this weighs a billion tons #shorts

More daily space Shorts: #Science #Space

NASA's Voyager lander passes tests, paving way for Moon Base's first lunar outpost with extreme space simulations.

#MoonBase #SpaceTech

Gravity and quantum info linked through Einstein's equations—spacetime shaped by quantum fields!

#QuantumPhysics #EinsteinEquations

Monocyte-derived galectin-1hi cells enhance memory CD8+ T cell function, boosting immune resilience. #Immunology #TCells

#ImmuneMemory #CellBiology

Did you know? Complex modes can form in lightly damped structures when two closely spaced modes interact via nonproportional damping.

#StructuralEngineering #VibrationAnalysis

What if dimming the Sun backfires? A solar geoengineering simulation reveals geopolitics could make climate chaos worse.

#ClimateGeoengineering #GlobalPolitics

A red dwarf is slowly devouring a brown dwarf, defying expectations in a 300-light-year cosmic feast.

#Astronomy #StellarEvolution

Who's responsible for AI-generated text in public debates? MIT researcher Deb Roy advocates for accountability in civic conversations.

#AIethics #PublicAccountability

Chile's "Desert Stairway to Heaven" offers a surreal blend of Earth and cosmos, perfect for stargazers.

#APOD #Stargazing

This week Curiosity rover returns to its regular schedule after a brief detour to study an erosional surface. The team is now back on track climbing Mount Sharp, gathering data to unravel Gale Crater’s geological history.

#CuriosityRover #MountSharp

AI‑powered papers are exploding, overwhelming volunteer reviewers. The piece details how the flood of submissions and complex methods strain traditional peer review, and asks if AI can help or replace human gatekeepers.

#PeerReview #AI

NASA is hosting a live news conference on Friday, Aug 14 at 2:30 p.m. EDT from the XLV Hangar at Kennedy Space Center’s Shuttle Landing Facility. Media and digital creators are invited on‑site to preview an upcoming NASA‑Kennedy event celebrating U.S. air‑and‑space leadership.

#NASA #AirSpaceLeadership

Sharp images from two giant Earth telescopes reveal asteroid (44) Nysa’s surface is split by two deep valleys that look like necks, linking three lobes into a single 75‑km body—potentially the first known triple‑lobed world. A hidden 1‑km moon was also spotted.

#Asteroid #ThreeLobes

Tonight's APOD captures the July "Buck Moon" soaring above a hazy horizon while the faint pink Belt of Venus glows just above the evening sky. The image highlights lunar illumination and Earth's atmospheric scattering, reminding us how our planet's thin veil paints twilight with delicate colors.

#BuckMoon #BeltOfVenus

ESA astronaut Sara García Alonso shows how to watch a solar eclipse safely—use certified eclipse glasses, never ordinary sunglasses. The video explains each eclipse phase, when it’s safe to look up, and why proper filters protect your eyes during this stunning cosmic show.

#SolarEclipse #SafeViewing

After a disaster, the timing of meals reshapes how fasting drives cravings. Using EEG beta‑band activity, researchers found that early refeeding blunts craving spikes seen after long fasts, while delayed feeding amplifies them. The study highlights brain‑wave markers linking nutrition timing to desire for food.

#FoodCraving #EEGResearch

Even at light‑speed limits, reaching the nearest star would take centuries with today’s tech. Researchers explore breakthroughs like nuclear pulse propulsion, antimatter drives, and solar sails powered by lasers—concepts that could slash travel time from millennia to decades.

#InterstellarTravel #NuclearRocket

New peptide‑centric local stability assay lets researchers map where small molecules bind across the whole proteome. By measuring changes in peptide thermal stability after ligand exposure, it pinpoints both protein targets and exact binding regions, accelerating drug discovery and chemical biology studies.

#Proteomics #DrugDiscovery

A new arXiv paper by Evann Kurzawa‑Ferrandez et al. shows how the ELT’s high‑resolution spectrograph could detect biosignature gases—like O₂, CH₄ and CO₂—in the atmospheres of nearby rocky exoplanets. Simulations indicate the 39‑m telescope will isolate faint planetary lines from stellar glare, offering a realistic route to spotting life‑related chemistry beyond Earth.

#Exoplanets #ELT

Tech firms are diversifying qubit hardware with fresh quantum‑dot designs (silicon, germanium) and diamond nitrogen‑vacancy defects. The new platforms promise longer coherence, tighter integration with existing chips, and a backup to superconducting & ion traps.

#QuantumComputing #Qubits

NASA’s Innovative Advanced Concepts program backs a bold new study by physicist Paul Stankus to use two tightly‑flying spacecraft as a giant camera. The formation could one day capture true images of an Earth‑like exoplanet—its oceans, continents and surface details—turning distant worlds from dots into visible landscapes.

#ExoplanetImaging #SpaceExploration

NASA's APOD for July 30 captures a deep‑red Sun filtered through massive wildfire smoke plumes over the western U.S. Fine ash and aerosols scatter blue light, leaving only long‑wavelength reds—a vivid reminder of how atmospheric particles can dim daylight, alter climate and affect astronomical observations.

#RedSun #WildfireSmoke

Born from MIT’s 1970s data system, PhysioNet launched 25 years ago and now powers the world’s largest open biomedical repository. It standardizes ECG, EEG, and ICU recordings, fuels AI research, and sets a global benchmark for secure, reproducible data sharing.

#PhysioNet #OpenScience

Superconducting qubits have gone from bulky lab curiosities to chip‑scale devices that fit in a palm. Advances in materials, 3‑D integration and error‑correction architectures now push coherence times past 0.5 ms and enable thousands of linked qubits, bringing practical quantum computers closer than ever.

#QuantumComputing #SuperconductingQubits

NASA’s Innovative Advanced Concepts program announced 18 new Phase‑I awards worth $3.2 M to fund visionary aerospace projects—from deep‑space propulsion and lunar habitats to novel telescopes and asteroid deflection concepts. Each team receives up to $175k for a nine‑month feasibility study.

#NIAC #SpaceTech

NASA’s Curiosity rover snapped Mastcam images of a newly‑named sand‑capped butte, “Miraflores,” about 6 m (20 ft) tall on Sol 4,923 (June 11, 2026). The isolated feature stands as surrounding rock eroded away, deepening the valley around it.

#MarsRover #Miraflores

NASA’s ESCAPADE (Escape & Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft, perched at the Sun‑Earth L2 point, sent back breathtaking “home‑views” – a full‑disk Earth shining with city lights and auroras alongside a crisp Moon in various phases. The images showcase our planet‑moon system from a stable, temporary orbit 1.5 million km away.

#ESCAPADE #Moon

Researchers show that rare‑earth ions embedded in crystals can serve as qubits that are controllable with standard telecom‑band lasers. The ions retain millisecond spin coherence while allowing optical links between neighboring qubits, paving the way for scalable quantum networks compatible with existing fiber infrastructure.

#QuantumTech #RareEarth

A newly-examined geometric shape that famously solved a century-old Einstein puzzle is now being probed for hidden traits. Researchers show its untapped properties could steer light into exotic chiral patterns, opening a pathway toward fresh physics insights beyond the original math triumph.

#Geometry #Photonics

NASA’s Swift rescue spacecraft has lost two of its three reaction wheels, leaving only a single wheel to control attitude. With precise pointing now at risk, engineers are scrambling for software work‑arounds while they diagnose the malfunction and explore backup options.

#SwiftMission #ReactionWheels

Rare cosmic collisions between wandering black holes and stray stars happen only every ~100 k years. When a star drifts too close, the supermassive black hole’s tidal forces spaghettify it, ripping off streams of gas that swirl into an accretion disk—an eerie, luminous death throe captured by astronomers.

#BlackHole #TidalDisruption

A new study shows that an Alu‑repeat‑driven deletion in the SPAST gene disrupts zinc handling in the Golgi, leading to neuronal stress. Restoring zinc balance with chelators rescues cells, uncovering a potential therapeutic target for hereditary spastic paraplegia.

#HereditarySpasticParaplegia #ZincTherapy

New IllustrisTNG simulations challenge the long‑standing view that galaxy mergers quench star formation. Instead of triggering powerful quasars that shut down stellar birth, merged galaxies often keep forming stars at normal or even elevated rates. The study suggests merger‑driven black‑hole feedback may be less decisive than thought.

#GalaxyMergers #StarFormation

Physicists at PSI tested a long‑standing mirror‑world hypothesis by watching 25 billion ultracold neutrons. Their data show no loss of neutrons into a hidden sector, effectively ruling out the idea that these particles vanish into a dark‑matter “mirror” universe.

#MirrorWorld #DarkMatter

Manchester scientists have shown that 'hot-electrons' generated by an ultra‑intense laser can remodel a metal's crystal structure within picoseconds—without heating the atomic lattice. The discovery reveals a non‑thermal pathway for reshaping metals, opening doors to ultrafast device engineering.

#HotElectrons #UltrafastMaterials

NASA engineers say current EVA suits are far too heavy for Mars’ 0.38 g gravity. A study presented at ICES shows next‑gen suits must shed about 40% of their mass to keep astronauts mobile and safe in the thin, cold atmosphere.

#MarsSuit #SpaceTech

Lightning storms have sparked dozens of wildfires across central and eastern Oregon, creating massive smoke plumes that drift over the state like a blanket. Scientists track how these emissions affect air quality, climate, and fire behavior.

#Wildfires #Oregon

JWST may finally let us see volcanic exomoons – “exo‑Ios” – around distant super‑Jupiters. Like Io, these moons would be torn by tidal heating, spewing lava and gases that travel along the planet’s magnetic field, lighting up aurorae. Detecting those glowing auroral signatures could reveal hidden worlds far beyond our solar system.

#ExoplanetScience #VolcanicMoons

Researchers unveiled a non‑contact sensing technique that gauges laser‑cutting depth during semiconductor wafer dicing by monitoring the recoil force generated when material vaporizes. Real‑time measurements enable tighter control of pulse energy and focus, boosting yield for delicate, low‑strength chips without mechanical stress.

#LaserDicing #SemiconductorManufacturing

NASA used the Aug 12 total solar eclipse over Greenland & Iceland to probe the Sun’s corona and its Earth impact. Spacecraft like Parker Solar Probe, SDO and IRIS gathered UV, magnetic and atmospheric data, while aircraft and ground teams measured changes—advancing space‑weather science.

#SolarEclipse #SpaceWeather

Warwick scientists propose a new quantum chip design that harnesses intrinsic mechanical vibrations—phonons to act as quantum buses, transmitting entanglement between far‑separated qubits on the same die. This built‑in phononic network could overcome wiring bottlenecks and scale up processors.

#QuantumComputing #PhononicQubits

NASA’s new Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to directly image and analyze Earth‑like exoplanets. The agency launched a Technology Maturation Project Office to sync engineering, optics, starlight suppression, and science goals. A detailed pre‑print roadmap outlines the milestones needed before the Mission Concept Review slated for decade’s end.

#HabitableWorlds #ExoplanetScience

NASA’s Hubble telescope reveals Andromeda’s stellar factories are slowing: star‑formation rates have dropped by ~50% over the past 500 million years, signaling the galaxy’s transition toward a quieter, “red‑and‑dead” future. The detailed UV‑optical survey maps this decline across its spiral arms.

#Andromeda #StarFormation

Physicists have finally observed a Floquet topological state— a light‑driven phase where a material’s bulk stays insulating while its surface conducts. Using intense, ultrafast laser pulses they reshaped the electronic bands of a crystal, delivering the first direct experimental proof of this theoretically predicted, non‑equilibrium topology.

#FloquetPhysics #TopologicalMatter

ASU researchers show that high‑altitude clouds in sub‑Neptune atmospheres act like thermal blankets, altering heat flow and causing the planet’s deep envelope to expand or contract. Their models link cloud opacity to measurable changes in radius and interior composition, reshaping how we interpret these common worlds.

#Exoplanets #CloudScience

New research shows black‑hole mergers can happen repeatedly in dense star clusters, where a freshly formed massive BH soon partners with another companion and collides again. Gravitational‑wave signatures reveal these “repeat” events, reshaping our view of cosmic evolution.

#BlackHoles #GravitationalWaves

Physicists tested a Josephson junction—a ultra‑precise quantum voltage‑to‑oscillation converter—just outside a black hole’s event horizon. They found that intense gravity skews the measured frequency for distant observers, but the underlying quantum law governing the circuit remains unchanged.

#BlackHolePhysics #QuantumDevices
